{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVfxoTs8AAAABiE1jhw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpzn1zhLcg70", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpzn1", "number": 13, "title": "Build reusable Rust/WASM SFC Studio tools for human and AI-assisted game development", "body": "## Goal
Build a reusable, game-agnostic Super Famicom asset authoring toolset for human and AI-assisted game development. The first intended use case is a future original RPG inspired by late-era SFC JRPG development workflows, but the tools must not depend on any specific game, genre, ROM layout, or engine.

## Architecture
- [ ] Create a Rust Cargo workspace under `tools/studio/` with shared library crates, a browser GUI (`web/`, Rust + WebAssembly; evaluate egui/eframe), and a native CLI (`cli/`).
- [ ] Keep editing, rendering, conversion, validation and serialization in shared Rust libraries; GUI and CLI call the same operations.
- [ ] Define documented, versioned, deterministic, Git-friendly asset formats (JSON, indexed PNG, WAV, etc.) with stable IDs and round-trip tests. Support browser import/export and project-directory workflows where supported, with portable file/ZIP fallback.
- [ ] Keep game-specific schemas, ROM packing and build logic in each game's own build tools; no game-specific adapters or dependencies inside Studio.
- [ ] Support static web hosting (e.g. GitHub Pages), without a required backend.

## Initial editor milestones
- [ ] Palette editor: BGR555, subpalettes, transparency and quantization.
- [ ] Pixel/tile editor: indexed graphics, 8x8 tiles, 2/4/8bpp preview and export.
- [ ] Metatile/tileset editor: configurable compositions, flip and palette attributes.
- [ ] Map editor: layers, tile placement, configurable metadata, selection, fill, copy/paste, undo/redo.
- [ ] Sprite and animation editor: OAM-compatible composition, frames, timing, previews and hardware validation.

## Follow-up milestones
- [ ] Bitmap font editor and general image conversion.
- [ ] BRR sample editor/converter, music and SFX editors with driver-independent authoring formats and previews.
- [ ] Compression/decompression, ROM-header inspection, VRAM layout visualization and hardware budget checks. Keep runtime-specific codecs/driver exporters outside generic editors as appropriate.
- [ ] Evaluate period SFC development workflows and modern reference tools; document which historical details are verified versus inferred.

## Human/AI collaboration
- [ ] Every core editing/validation/rendering operation should be callable programmatically through the shared library and, where practical, CLI.
- [ ] Provide structured JSON diagnostics, deterministic noninteractive commands, meaningful exit codes, help/examples, and dry-run/diff support for edits.
- [ ] Support rendering maps, sprites, palettes and other assets to PNG so humans and AI can inspect results.
- [ ] Document a round trip: AI creates or modifies assets via CLI or files; human edits the same assets in the browser; AI reads the exported changes, validates and renders them. No silent overwriting of human changes.
- [ ] Add a small standalone fixture project and automated native/WASM parity, round-trip, deterministic export and validation tests.
- [ ] CLI-first: do not require AI integration, model APIs, MCP or an AI backend to use Studio. Evaluate optional MCP only after practical CLI workflows are established.

## Scope and constraints
Do not create or modify a game, its content, existing ROMs, or existing build pipelines as part of initial Studio implementation. Use standalone original test fixtures. Existing games must continue building unchanged. The new RPG engine and game-specific tools/content will be separate tasks. Use independent implementations and appropriately licensed assets.
